cues.caption: Chapter 2 · Probability
cues.text: Today is chapter two of Problem Solver. It's called, Probability. What are the chances?

cues.caption: Probability = chance. How likely is it?
cues.text: Probability sounds like a huge word, doesn't it? But it just means chance. How likely is something to happen? Let's find out!

cues.caption: Meet Aarav, playing Ludo with Nani
cues.text: Meet Aarav. Every Sunday, he plays Ludo with his nani. And Nani is very hard to beat!

cues.caption: "Please be a six!"
cues.text: In Ludo, you need a six to move your first piece out. Aarav shakes the die, and whispers, please be a six!

cues.caption: A six on the first roll? Think!
cues.text: Will Aarav get a six on his very first roll? What do you think? Yes, or no?

cues.caption: Nobody knows for sure, but we know how likely
cues.text: Here's the honest answer. Nobody knows for sure! It might be a six. It might not. But we can still say how likely it is. And that's what probability is all about.

cues.caption: Probability = the chance something happens
cues.text: Probability means the chance that something will happen. Not what will happen. Just how likely it is.

cues.caption: Impossible → Unlikely → Likely → Certain
cues.text: We can put chances on a chance line. At one end is impossible. Then comes unlikely, then likely. And at the other end, certain.

cues.caption: Never · Probably not · Probably · Surely
cues.text: Impossible means it can never happen. Unlikely means it could happen, but probably won't. Likely means it will probably happen. And certain means it will surely happen.

cues.caption: The sun will rise tomorrow → certain
cues.text: Let's try some. The sun will rise tomorrow. That happens every single day, so it's certain.

cues.caption: Roll a 7 on a normal die → impossible
cues.text: Rolling a seven on a normal die? A die only has the numbers one to six. There is no seven! So that's impossible.

cues.caption: A 6 on the first roll: 1 out of 6 → unlikely
cues.text: Now, Aarav's six on the first roll. A six is just one face out of six. It could happen, but it probably won't. So it's unlikely.

cues.caption: Smaller than 6: 5 out of 6 → likely
cues.text: And rolling any number smaller than six? One, two, three, four, or five. That's five faces out of six. So that's likely!

cues.caption: The cricket toss: heads or tails?
cues.text: Now, think of a cricket match. Before it starts, the captains toss a coin. Heads, or tails?

cues.caption: Heads: 1 out of 2 · Tails: 1 out of 2
cues.text: A coin has two sides. Heads is one side out of two. Tails is one side out of two. Same chance!

cues.caption: Lots of tosses → about half and half
cues.text: So heads and tails are equally likely. If you toss a coin ten times, you might not get exactly five heads. But over lots of tosses, it comes out about half and half.

cues.caption: Fair = every result has the same chance
cues.text: That's why the toss is fair. Fair means every result has the same chance. Nobody gets a head start!

cues.caption: 6 faces · each number is 1 out of 6
cues.text: A normal die is fair too. It has six faces, so each number has a chance of one out of six.

cues.caption: Chance of an even number? Count!
cues.text: Here's one for you. What's the chance of rolling an even number? Count the even faces. Take your time.

cues.caption: Even: 2, 4, 6 → 3 out of 6
cues.text: The even numbers are two, four, and six. That's three faces. So the chance is three out of six. That's half the faces!

cues.caption: 7 blue marbles and 3 yellow marbles
cues.text: Nani has a cloth bag of marbles. Seven blue marbles, and three yellow marbles. She gives it a good shake.

cues.caption: Chance of yellow? Likely or unlikely?
cues.text: Aarav picks one without looking. What's the chance it's yellow? And is that likely, or unlikely? Pause and think.

cues.caption: Yellow: 3 out of 10 · Blue: 7 out of 10
cues.text: First, count them all. Seven plus three makes ten marbles. Three are yellow, so the chance is three out of ten. That's unlikely. And blue? Seven out of ten. That's likely!

cues.caption: No red marbles → red is impossible
cues.text: Now a new bag, with five green marbles, and no red ones at all. Picking a red marble? Impossible! There are none. And picking green? Certain!

cues.caption: 4 equal parts → fair
cues.text: Spinners can be fair, or unfair. This spinner has four equal parts, each a different colour. Every colour has the same chance. That's fair.

cues.caption: 3 red, 1 blue → red is more likely
cues.text: This one has four equal parts too, but three are red, and only one is blue. Red has three parts out of four. So red is more likely!

cues.caption: One part is half the circle. Fair?
cues.text: And look at this one. One part is half of the whole circle! Is this spinner fair? Think about it.

cues.caption: Not fair! Fair spinners have equal parts
cues.text: Not fair! The big part takes up half the circle, so the arrow stops there much more often. Fair spinners have equal parts.

cues.caption: AI uses chance too!
cues.text: Here's something cool. AI uses chance too!

cues.caption: Seen lots of cats → pointy ears? Likely a cat
cues.text: Remember how AI learns from examples? If it has seen a hundred cat photos with pointy ears, then a new photo with pointy ears is likely a cat.

cues.caption: "Happy…" → "birthday" is most likely
cues.text: Your phone does it too. Type, happy, and it suggests, birthday. It picks the word that's most likely to come next.

cues.caption: Most likely is not certain. AI can be wrong!
cues.text: But AI is not always certain. It picks what's most likely, and sometimes, it guesses wrong. Just like us!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Rolling a 7: impossible or unlikely? Why?
cues.text: Is rolling a seven on a normal die impossible, or unlikely? And why? Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: Impossible! A die only has 1 to 6
cues.text: Impossible! A normal die only has the numbers one to six. So a seven can never come up, not even once. Did you get it? Brilliant!

cues.caption: Impossible → unlikely → likely → certain
cues.text: Let's remember. Chances go from impossible, to unlikely, to likely, to certain.

cues.caption: Coin: heads and tails equally likely
cues.text: A coin has two sides, so heads and tails are equally likely.

cues.caption: Fair = every result, same chance
cues.text: Fair means every result has the same chance, like a normal die, or a spinner with equal parts.

cues.caption: AI picks the most likely, from examples
cues.text: And AI picks what's most likely, from lots of examples.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 done!
cues.text: Chapter two, done! You can talk about chances like a pro, champ.
